messages:
alex: Heads up — during the eu-west-1 nightly scale we hit a registration failure when new GPU nodes join the private NLB target groups. Autoscaler spins up 6 g5 instances and a bunch of targets fail to register with error LimitExceeded. Can someone open a request for increasing NLB target attachments and interface endpoints per VPC?

ruth: Which AWS account / VPC / ASG sizes? Any recent config changes?

alex: Account: 111222333444, VPC: vpc-0a1b2c3d, ASG: inference-gpu-eu (desired=18, max=24). Error snippet from controller logs: 
```
2026-03-18T02:10:12Z controller: register-targets failed (LimitExceeded): Cannot register targets: exceed target count for load balancer
attempted_register=12 current_count=4998 limit=5000
```
We also have ~320 interface endpoints in that VPC (mostly private model-serving endpoints).

sam: Looks like we hit the soft limit for "Targets per Network Load Balancer" in that region/account + interface endpoint limit. File a support case requesting bump to at least 15000 targets and interface endpoints to 500. Include justification: autoscaling for GPU pools, short burst capacity, low risk because it's for private infra. I'll paste example payload.

sam: Example console request body: 
```
Service: EC2
Limit: Network Load Balancer - Targets per NLB
Region: eu-west-1
Current: 5000
Requested: 15000
Reason: Inference GPU autoscaling (reserved pools + burst). Expected peak target registrations per hour: ~7k. Contact: infra@redwood.ai
```

lee: I'll open the support ticket and loop in our cloud account rep. @cloud-rep can we get an expedited review? This is causing ~5% error rate on tail latency for production batches.

cloud-rep: Thanks @lee — I've acknowledged. Quick notes: AWS typically asks for traffic justification + expected monthly metrics. I can push for a soft-limit temporary bump to 8000 while they evaluate. Please attach ASG history and a short architecture diagram showing why targets scale with node count.

alex: Attached ASG activity and a tiny diagram in the ticket. Also adding cost/usage note: we only register private endpoints from nodes during startup, steady state registers are lower. Bump to 8000 would avoid outages while they do full review.

infra-bot: Incident created: #INC-20260318-88 (NLB target registration failures). Pager duty suppressed, severity: P2.

lee: Cloud replied: initial soft bump approved to 8000 for 72 hours, they requested the monthly peak estimate and a runbook for node join/fail behavior. I've updated the ticket and asked for permanent increase.

alex: Great, thanks. Will add a guard in autoscaler to limit concurrent batch register operations to avoid a repeat.

ruth: Can we also look at consolidating some interface endpoints (VPC endpoints) — looks like we have duplicated service endpoints across stacks. Might reduce count.

sam: Agree — I'll run an inventory script and surface duplication. For now, plan: (1) autoscaler throttle, (2) cloud rep temp bump to 8000, (3) cleanup plan for endpoints.

lee: Closing loop — ticket updates in console, keeping thread open until permanent limit is confirmed. :thumbsup:
